Interest was stated to be charged at 29.99 - 34.99 %, but that only totals {$2300.00} max ). Currently XXXX  and had some family issues around this time, so we missed the ending of this promo. In XXXX XXXX, we saw that we had been charged the almost $ XXXX in interest, plus being charged interest of ~ {$140.00} each month, despite still auto paying more than the minimum payment. Called Synchrony Bank on XX/XX/XXXX to get this resolved and told that we were informed multiple times that the promo was ending ( we in fact were not told multiple times but instead a very small disclaimer on one statement in XX/XX/XXXX mentioned it in a confusing way - attached in screenshots what was said about the promo balance ), and that we missed the grace period to get interest reversed ( grace period not mentioned anywhere on the statement or online, and rep from Synchrony flat out told us that they don't tell people about this grace period at all, we are just supposed to know ). Spoke with a bank manager on XX/XX/XXXX who let us know that they would file a dispute to get the interest charges looked at for reversal and let us know via email in 7-10 business days. On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a dispute with Bank of America for two transactions made on my credit card. These transactions together represented a single order with the merchant, XXXX XXXX. The first transaction was the initial deposit, and the second was the final payment. The order was managed through XXXX, a marketplace platform similar to XXXX XXXX, which facilitates communication between buyers and sellers but does not directly handle transactions. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a request from Bank of America to submit documentation supporting my claim. I promptly provided all requested details along with a 32-page comprehensive document that included extensive evidence, such as written confirmation from the vendor ( XXXX XXXX ) acknowledging multiple issues with the order, including missing products and defects. Despite this thorough submission, on XX/XX/XXXX, I received another request for additional documents. Upon reviewing this new request, I noticed that most of the information being asked for had already been submitted in my initial filing. 

I contacted the dispute department on XX/XX/XXXX ( call logged at XXXXXXXX XXXX ) to address this issue. During the call, the representative confirmed that all required documents were indeed submitted with my initial response and that no further documentation was needed. However, to expedite the case, I recompiled the requested materials and submitted them again, organized in the format specified in the second request. 

Despite my efforts, on XX/XX/XXXX, I received a final decision letter from the bank stating that my claim had been denied. The reason provided was that the funds were deducted by XXXX, not XXXX XXXX, making any documentation from the vendor irrelevant. However, this rationale is flawed for several reasons : XXXX. XXXX XXXX : XXXX serves as a payment processor ( similar to XXXX or XXXX ) and a communication platform but is not the merchant in this transaction. The vendor, XXXX XXXX, used XXXX XXXX  XXXX  to charge my card. 
XXXX. Vendor Admissions : The vendor has explicitly acknowledged the issues with the order, including missing products and defects, in writing, which I submitted as part of my evidence. 
XXXX. Inconsistent Rationale : The bank dismissed my vendor-related evidence by claiming that XXXX collected the funds and is therefore the merchant of record. However, when I proposed changing my claim to reflect that XXXX failed to deliver any product, the bank stated that product issues must be addressed with the vendor. This contradictory stance undermines the legitimacy of their decision. 
I believe Bank of America failed to thoroughly review the evidence I provided. The decision to disregard the vendors admissions of fault and to incorrectly assign responsibility to XXXX is both unreasonable and unjustified. The role of XXXX as a payment processor should not obscure the fact that the claim is between myself and XXXX XXXX, the actual merchant. 

I request that the CFPB compel Bank of America to conduct a fair and thorough review of my claim, focusing on the evidence provided and disregarding the irrelevant role of XXXX as a payment processor. If the bank continues to treat XXXX as the merchant, it must provide proof that XXXX delivered the products in question. 

This matter involves a significant financial amount, and I can not accept being defrauded without receiving the products I paid for. I ask for your assistance in ensuring that my claim is reviewed properly and justly resolved.

XX/XX/year>2025 Dear CFPB, I am writing to file a formal complaint against the Military Department of Chase Bank, specifically regarding their refusal to honor the protections provided under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ) [ 50 U.S.C. 3937 ] and related state laws, as well as their discriminatory and unprofessional treatment of service members. 

Background I am a XXXX XXXX XXXX member and a resident of California. My ship date to Basic Combat Training ( BCT ) is XX/XX/year>2025, and my training, including Advanced Individual Training ( AIT ), will extend until XX/XX/scrub> 2025. Both BCT and AIT are classified as XXXX XXXX under 10 U.S.C. 101 ( d ) ( 1 ) and Department of Defense directives. 

These periods of service entitle me to protections under the SCRA and California Military and Veterans Code 405, including the right to request a reduction in my credit card interest rate during my active-duty period. 

Issues with Chase Banks Military Department When I contacted Chase Banks Military Department, I encountered the following issues that demonstrate systemic problems within their organization : Misinformation Regarding XXXX XXXX Status : A Chase employee named XXXX incorrectly stated that BCT and AIT do not qualify as XXXX XXXX. When I provided legal definitions under 10 U.S.C. 101 ( d ) ( 1 ) and explained that these trainings are explicitly recognized as XXXX XXXX by the Department of Defense, she dismissed my explanation and responded with hostility. 
Her exact words were : If you want to, go ahead and do whatever you want. Either way, we wont approve it. 

This statement reflects a lack of understanding of military laws and a dismissive attitude toward service members. 

Unreasonable Documentation Requirements : Despite SCRA provisions allowing alternative forms of documentation ( e.g., a letter from my commanding officer, 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( b ) ( 1 ) ), Chase Banks Military Department insisted that I provide my official military orders. 
Military orders are typically issued only days before the ship date, leaving insufficient time for processing. I explained that I would not be able to follow up during BCT due to communication restrictions, but Chase employees showed no flexibility or willingness to accommodate this situation. 
Procedural Barriers and Unfair Treatment : When I asked if I could submit my orders after departure without restarting the process, XXXX stated that I would need to resubmit all documents and restart the 30-day processing period. 
This rigid approach is inconsistent with SCRAs intent to provide timely and accessible protections for service members. 
Discriminatory and Hostile Conduct : XXXX tone and dismissive comments reflect a systemic lack of respect and understanding toward service members. Her statements suggest a discriminatory attitude and targeted behavior against those seeking military-related benefits. 
Legal Violations The actions of Chase Banks Military Department violate the following laws : Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ), 50 U.S.C. 3937 : Failing to honor valid active-duty status during BCT and AIT. 
Refusing to accept alternative documentation permitted under federal law. 
California Military and Veterans Code 405 : Imposing unnecessary barriers and delays that infringe upon the rights of California service members.

10 U.S.C. 101 ( d ) ( 1 ) : Misinterpreting BCT and AIT as not qualifying as XXXX XXXX, contrary to explicit federal definitions. 
12 U.S.C. 5531 ( UDAAP ) : The dismissive and hostile treatment by Chase Bank employees constitutes an unfair, deceptive, and abusive practice against military personnel.

38 U.S.C. 4311 : Prohibits discrimination against service members based on their military status. Chase Banks hostile treatment and procedural rigidity reflect bias against military enlistees. 
Request for Action Chase Banks Military Department has failed to provide the professionalism, respect, and compliance required by law. I urge the CFPB to : Investigate Chase Banks Military Department : Ensure their policies and employee training comply with the SCRA, including proper recognition of active-duty status for BCT and AIT.

Enforce Procedural Reforms : Require Chase Bank to accept alternative documentation such as letters from commanding officers, as outlined in 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( b ) ( 1 ).

Address Discriminatory Behavior : Mandate sensitivity and compliance training for Chase Banks Military Department employees to prevent further discriminatory or hostile conduct.

Ensure Timely Processing for Service Members : Establish clear guidelines to process military benefit requests without unnecessary delays or barriers, particularly for service members with restricted communication during training.

Thank you for addressing this urgent matter. I am available to provide supporting documentation and further details upon request. I trust that the CFPB will take appropriate action to uphold the rights and dignity of service members and ensure accountability within Chase Banks Military Department.

Sincerely,

According to IRS regulations, when a creditor writes off a debt as a loss, they are required to furnish the debtor with a Form 1099-C to report the canceled debt as income. This allows the debtor to accurately report the income on their taxes. 

Goldman Sachs Apple Card 's failure to provide me with a 1099-C is concerning, as it prevents me from fulfilling my tax obligations correctly. I believe I am entitled to receive this form promptly so that I may include it in my tax filings. 

Furthermore, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), creditors are required to provide accurate information regarding debts. Incorrectly reporting a charged-off debt as an outstanding balance on my credit report while claiming a tax loss could constitute inaccurate reporting.

If Goldman Sachs Apple Card does not furnish me with the Form 1099-C or remove the accounts from my credit report due to inaccurate reporting promptly, I am prepared to pursue legal action for statutory damages. This situation is causing undue stress and financial uncertainty. 

I kindly request your assistance in directing Goldman Sachs Apple Card to fulfill their legal obligation by providing me with the necessary Form 1099-C for the charged-off accounts. Please advise me on how best to proceed in resolving this matter.

records.narrative:
Hello. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a promotional email from Wells Fargo about a 0 % APR for 12 months on balance transfers and 29.99 % variable after that. Since I have other balances to other creditors that I was looking to transfer, I called Wells Fargo to learn more about the promotion and to ask how my payments will be applied should I move forward with availing the promotion. On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a Wells Fargo agent who confirmed that, if my payment is not equal to my statement balance, it will be applied to the highest APR first before the lower APR. I then asked, given that the balance transfer is at 0 % APR ( for the first 12 months ), does that mean that the balance transfer balance will always be last in the order of priority when they apply my payments. The agent confirmed Yes. After that call, on XX/XX/XXXX, I transferred my balance in my XXXX account to Wells Fargo in the amount of {$1200.00}. I was charged {$60.00} transfer fee for the transfer. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received my billing statement ending XX/XX/XXXX, with a statement balance of {$3900.00}, due on XX/XX/XXXX, broken down as follows : {$2600.00} for card purchases, and {$1200.00} for balance transfer and fee. 
I do not have enough to pay the entire balance so I made sure to come up with at least more than {$2600.00} with the information they gave me that when my payment is not enough to cover the full statement balance, it will be applied to the highest APR first and then to the lower APR, and the balance transfer last.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I made another balance transfer to payoff my XXXX card balance amounting to {$780.00}. I was charged {$39.00} for the transfer. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I paid {$2700.00}, thinking that {$2600.00} will be applied to my credit card purchases, and {$150.00} to the balance transfer. I thought that because the card purchases are prioritized in payment application, I will not incur any interest because I am paying more than the card purchases balance. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I received my statement balance ending XX/XX/XXXX and to my surprise, I saw that Wells Fargo applied {$190.00} towards my balance transfer, and {$2500.00} to my card purchases balance. As such, I was left with balance on my card purchase. I was charged {$45.00} interest for a balance of {$1700.00} in my statement that I don't know how they arrived at. 
I called Wells Fargo on XX/XX/XXXX to complain about the interest fee showing on my XX/XX/XXXX statement, and the second agent I spoke with told me that the agent who told me that the balance transfer will always be last in the hierarchy of payment application is wrong, because their system will automatically and will always allocate a portion of the payment towards the balance transfer, even though it would mean that the card purchases balance will not be fully paid first. I was told that unfortunately, they don't have a control over how their system allocates payment, and even if I call prior to paying to inform them how I want my payment applied, they have no way of adjusting that. The agent I spoke with opened a case complaint for me for another team to review further. On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo called me and said they reviewed the XX/XX/XXXX conversation I had with their agent and they said based on their review, everything on their end was in order. 
I opened an account with another bank and initiated a balance transfer for all my balance with Wells Fargo as I do not want anything to do with them anymore. However, I would like to request your assistance in looking into this as I feel like I was defrauded. It is only {$45.00} interest, but to think about it, I was okay with paying them the balance transfer fee because I thought the 0 % promotional offer was a good deal. 
Thank you for your assistance.

Subject : Complaint Against Chase Card Services Failure to Provide Required Documentation and Violations of FCRA, ECOA, and TILA 1. Summary of Complaint I am submitting this complaint regarding Chase Card Services, which recently reduced my credit limit without proper justification and failed to provide the required documentation supporting their decision. I believe this constitutes violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), and Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ).

Despite my formal request for documentation, the company refused to provide details about the internal factors or credit-related items used to justify the limit reduction. This refusal violates my right to transparency under federal laws, particularly where adverse actions and credit report information are concerned.

2. Key Facts - Account Information : Chase Freedom - Date of Adverse Action : XX/XX/scrub> 2025 - Initial Request for Documentation : I called on XX/XX/scrub> 2025 and spoke with agent XXXX and requested detailed records of their decision making process instead of the vague generic information provided. 
- Issuers Response : Agent XXXX denied my request outright and provided incomplete/vague information about the decision. 
3. Violations Committed by Chase Card Services a. Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681m ( a ) Under the FCRA, Chase is required to provide an adverse action notice when a decision, such as a credit limit reduction, is based on information in my credit report. They failed to provide the following mandatory items as part of the notice : - The specific reasons for the limit reduction ( not generic terms ).

b. Violation of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) The ECOA requires creditors to provide consumers with a written statement explaining the reasons for adverse credit decisions. Chase response : - Provided a vague, generic reason, such as number of accounts currently in use or balances too high compared to credit limit, which is insufficient under ECOA guidelines.

Additionally, I am aware that creditors are obligated to keep records of their decision-making process and provide this information upon request, which has been denied to me.

c. Violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Regulation Z 15 U.S.C. 1637 ( b ) Under TILA, any significant change to my account, including a reduction of my credit limit, requires advance notice of at least 45 days, particularly if it involves a change in terms. I received notice in mail on XX/XX/year>2025 and notice dated on XXXX XXXX2025 as of today XX/XX/scrub> 2025 the credit limit has already been reduced meaning 45 days advance notice not given. Furthermore, the notice lacked critical details regarding how this reduction impacts my account balance, interest rates, and repayment obligations.

4. Requested Resolution I am requesting that the CFPB take the following actions to resolve this complaint : a. Full accounting and documentation under double-entry principles : - Provide a full breakdown of the internal decision-making process, including : - Credit report items, scores, and metrics considered.

- Internal risk models, scoring systems, or policies applied.

- Any financial adjustments recorded internally under double-entry bookkeeping, showing how the limit reduction was accounted for in their ledger.

Specifically, I am requesting the debit and credit journal entries that reflect the following : Debits ( Dr ) for any increased risk or losses they associated with my account.

Credits ( Cr ) for any offsetting benefits or gains resulting from the limit reduction.

b. Credit restoration : - Restore my previous credit limit immediately to prevent further damage to my credit utilization ratio and credit score.

- Remove any negative notations or adjustments to my credit profile caused by the limit reduction.

c. Monetary compensation : - Compensate me for financial and emotional harm, including : - Damages to my credit score and borrowing power.

- Higher credit utilization leading to potentially increased interest rates on future loans.

- Time and effort spent resolving this issue.

5. Supporting Documents I have attached the following documents to support my complaint : - Copy of any adverse action notice received - Screenshot the credit limited showing todays date XX/XX/year>2025 6. Impact of the Credit Limit Reduction This limit reduction has negatively impacted my financial situation and credit score due to the sudden increase in my credit utilization ratio. I believe that Chases refusal to provide documentation reflects a broader failure in transparency and regulatory compliance.

7. Conclusion I am seeking the CFPBs intervention to ensure that Chase complies with federal laws and provides the documentation and disclosures I am entitled to. Their noncompliance has not only affected my financial standing but also deprived me of my rights under the FCRA, ECOA, and TILA.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. Please let me know if you require any additional documentation to support this complaint.

Dear CFPB, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding a fraudulent credit account that was opened in my name with XXXX XXXX  Card Services. Upon discovering this fraudulent activity, I disputed the account. As a result, XXXXXXXX XXXX confirmed in writing that the account would be closed and removed from my credit report. 

Despite this confirmation, I have continued to receive multiple emails and phone calls attempting to collect on this fraudulent debt. Each time, I have provided the attached letter from XXXXXXXX XXXX verifying that the account was fraudulent and should not be pursued. However, I am now facing legal action from an attorney representing this debt, who is threatening to garnish my wages. 

The following laws are applicable to my case and should be enforced : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ) Ensures the accuracy and privacy of consumer credit reports. Under the FCRA : I have the right to dispute inaccurate information on my credit report ( 1681i ).
